# The map

*Generated by `pipeline/build_taxonomy.py` from `content/taxonomy/`. Do not edit this file; edit the realm outlines and rebuild.*

**1070 decisions** across 16 realms, 85 fields and 231 families. 154 are built (14.4 per cent of those in scope), 901 are open for work, 12 are held with a reason, and 3 are refused with a reason.

This is the map, not the navigation. `content/ontology.json` is what the site can show today. The gap between the two is the work, and publishing it as a number is the point: a catalogue that shows only what it has built looks finished when it is nine per cent done.

## Coverage against COICOP 2018

COICOP 2018 is the United Nations classification of what individuals consume. It is used here as an outside referee, so that "the map covers everything" is a check somebody else can run rather than a claim this project makes about itself.

## The realms

### Food and drink

*Everything eaten or drunk, where it is bought, and where it is eaten. Food grown at home belongs here; the tools for growing it belong to Home. Food for animals belongs to Animals. Infant formula belongs to Family and care, because the decision there is about feeding a baby, not about groceries.*

## Everything held or refused, with its reason

A catalogue that silently omits things looks incomplete. A catalogue that names what it will not do, and why, can be argued with. These are the arguable ones.

**Water at home** (Food and drink, held)

The decision here is a water supplier or a filter, and both are already decisions in Home. This line exists so the map does not imply drinking water is only something you buy in a bottle.

**Tobacco and cigarettes** (Food and drink, refused)

The catalogue ranks options inside a decision so a reader can choose a better one. There is no better cigarette on the axes this site measures, and building the comparison would dress a health decision as a values decision. Named here so its absence is a position rather than an oversight.

**Vapes and nicotine pouches** (Food and drink, refused)

Same reason as tobacco. The environmental case for a rechargeable vape over a disposable one is real, and it belongs in a guide about waste rather than in a ranking that would read as a recommendation to buy either.

**Independent restaurants and cafes** (Food and drink, held)

Ranking individual local restaurants needs local data the catalogue does not have and could not keep fresh. The useful unit here is a guide to reading a menu and a kitchen, not a national league table.

**Foraging** (Food and drink, held)

There is nothing to compare and nothing to buy. This belongs in a guide, and it sits on the map so that the free way of getting food is visible next to the paid ones.

**Abortion services and support** (Health, held)

This is a decision about access and care rather than a product to compare, and the honest instrument is a directory of what is lawful and available in a place, held by an organisation equipped to keep it accurate and safe. Named on the map so its absence is visible.

**Complementary and alternative therapies** (Health, held)

The catalogue can honestly compare a provider on price, ownership, data handling and complaints, and cannot rank a therapy that has no accepted evidence base without appearing to endorse it. Held until the measures can separate the provider from the claim.

**Walking and wheeling routes** (Transport, held)

There is no purchase and no provider to rank. It is on the map because a catalogue of how people move that starts at buying a car has already answered the question badly.

**AI training data and consent** (Technology, held)

There is nothing here a reader buys, and the question of whose work a model was trained on decides several rankings elsewhere in the catalogue. It sits on the map as a measure to be applied to AI decisions rather than as a decision of its own.

**Betting and gambling services** (Media and culture, refused)

A ranking implies the reader should pick one, and there is no version of this that serves a person better than not starting. The catalogue's values axes would also flatter the largest operators, whose compliance teams are the best resourced. Named so the refusal is visible and arguable rather than silent.

**Flight emissions and offsetting** (Travel, held)

Offsetting is a contested product and the honest comparison is between flying and not flying, or between a flight and a train. The catalogue can rank offset providers on integrity, and will not do so until it can say plainly that buying one is not the same as not emitting.

**Hotels** (Travel, held)

State attorney general settlements over hidden resort fees, and government labor and ADA findings, are real but they measure who got caught rather than current conduct: they track a chain's size and visibility more than its behaviour, so an axis built only from them would have put unsued brands at the top of a column that reads as good. The honest primary measure is whether a chain's own booking flow shows the total price, mandatory fees included, at first display, which is checkable for every brand today rather than only the ones with a public record. It could not be gathered that way: the booking search or results page for ten of the twelve brands considered (Marriott, Hilton, Hyatt, IHG, Choice, Motel 6, Red Roof Inn, Best Western, Extended Stay America, Radisson) returned an error to a plain fetch and to one with a full browser header, and only two (Wyndham, Omni) served a readable page at all, of which only Wyndham's said anything about fee inclusion. Held until that evidence can be gathered directly, in a browser, for most of the roster; the enforcement history remains worth keeping as a separate, clearly labelled record once the primary axis can carry its own weight.

**Volunteering trips** (Travel, held)

The sector contains real placements and real harm, and telling them apart needs local judgement the catalogue cannot supply from a distance. Held until a partner with that judgement can stand behind the comparison.

**Crypto mining and staking** (Money, held)

The measures that matter here are energy use and custody risk, and both change faster than the catalogue can currently keep a ranking honest. Held rather than published stale.

**Breeders and sellers** (Animals, held)

A ranking here would read as a shortlist of places to buy an animal, and the catalogue's position is that adoption comes first. What can be published honestly is what a lawful, welfare-first sale looks like, which is a guide rather than a comparison.
